title: C'est
subtitle: Saying it is / this is
explanation: Use c'est to say it is, this is, or that is before a description or noun.

title: Être: est / sont
subtitle: Is and are
explanation: Use est for is and sont for are. These are forms of être, one of the most important French verbs.

title: Definite articles: le, la, les, l’
subtitle: Saying the
explanation: Use le for masculine singular nouns, la for feminine singular nouns, les for plural nouns, and l’ before a vowel sound.

examples.fre: De cette vie qui les ronge,

title: Indefinite articles: un, une, des
subtitle: Saying a, an, some
explanation: Use un with masculine singular nouns, une with feminine singular nouns, and des with plural nouns.

examples.fre: Une vie où on serait deux,

title: De / d’ / du / de la / des
subtitle: Of, from, and some
explanation: Use de for of/from. It changes with articles: de + le becomes du, de + les becomes des, and de becomes d’ before a vowel sound.

examples.fre: De cette vie qui les ronge,
L’âme posée sur le mémoire de forme,
J’ai dû prendre de mon père,

title: Adjective agreement
subtitle: bon/bonne, parfait/parfaite
explanation: French adjectives often change to match the noun. Many add -e for feminine and -s for plural.

title: Possessive adjectives: mon, ma, mes, ton, votre
subtitle: Saying my, your
explanation: Use mon, ma, mes and other possessive adjectives before nouns to show ownership. The form depends on the noun.

examples.fre: J’ai dû prendre de mon père,

title: Je voudrais
subtitle: Polite I would like
explanation: Use je voudrais to make polite requests. It is softer than je veux.

title: Quel / quelle questions
subtitle: Asking which / what
explanation: Use quel before masculine nouns and quelle before feminine nouns when asking what or which.

title: Time expressions
subtitle: heures, et demie, et quart
explanation: Use heure(s) for o’clock times. Et demie means half past, et quart means quarter past, and moins le quart means quarter to.

title: Numbers and quantities
subtitle: deux, trois, cinq
explanation: Numbers are used before nouns for quantities, times, prices, and people.

examples.fre: Une vie où on serait deux,

title: Pronouns: moi, lui, elle
subtitle: For me, him, her
explanation: Use moi for me, lui for him, and elle for her after prepositions like pour and avec.

examples.fre: Je suis loin de chez moi

title: Reflexive verbs
subtitle: je me lève, je me lave
explanation: Reflexive verbs use me, te, se, nous, or vous before the verb when the action comes back to the subject.

title: Present tense verbs
subtitle: Everyday actions now
explanation: Use the present tense to talk about current facts, routines, and repeated actions.

title: Near future: aller + infinitive
subtitle: Going to do something
explanation: Use aller plus an infinitive to say someone is going to do something: je vais faire, nous allons nettoyer.

title: Infinitives after helper verbs
subtitle: vouloir, pouvoir, aller + verb
explanation: After verbs like vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, and aller, the next verb often stays in the infinitive form.

title: Passé composé
subtitle: Completed past actions
explanation: Use passé composé for completed actions in the past. It often uses avoir or être plus a past participle.

examples.fre: J’ai dû prendre de mon père,

title: Imparfait
subtitle: Background past actions
explanation: Use imparfait for past background, descriptions, habits, or ongoing actions.

examples.fre: On mangeait en silence devant la télé,

title: Conditional
subtitle: Would / could
explanation: The conditional often expresses would, could, or imagined situations, such as je voudrais or on aurait.

examples.fre: Une vie où on serait deux,

title: Relative pronouns: qui / que / où
subtitle: Joining ideas
explanation: Use qui, que, and où to connect two ideas: who/that, that/which, or where.

examples.fre: De cette vie qui les ronge,
Une vie où on serait deux,

title: Negation: ne...pas / ne...plus / ne...rien
subtitle: Making sentences negative
explanation: French negatives often wrap around the verb: ne...pas, ne...plus, ne...jamais, or ne...rien.

title: Connectors: et, mais, puis, après
subtitle: Joining and sequencing ideas
explanation: Use connectors like et, mais, puis, ensuite, après, and quand to join ideas and show order.

title: Adverbs: très, toujours, bientôt
subtitle: Adding detail
explanation: Adverbs such as très, toujours, bientôt, directement, and généralement add more detail to verbs or adjectives.

title: Chez
subtitle: At someone’s place
explanation: Use chez to mean at someone’s home/place or at a professional’s office, such as chez moi or chez le médecin.

examples.fre: Je suis loin de chez moi

title: Par
subtitle: By / per
explanation: Use par to mean by or per, especially with prices and payment expressions.

title: Location descriptions
subtitle: à gauche, à droite, en face
explanation: Use location expressions to describe where things are in a room or place.

title: Faire expressions
subtitle: faire le ménage, faire les courses
explanation: Faire is used in many common expressions, especially for chores, activities, and shopping.

title: Prendre
subtitle: Taking / having
explanation: Prendre can mean to take or to have, especially with meals, transport, or breaks.

examples.fre: J’ai dû prendre de mon père,

title: Aller
subtitle: Going
explanation: Aller means to go. It is also used to build the near future with another infinitive.
